notes: An official support reply recommends MBR with FAT32 or HFS+ for an export drive.
This supports a conditional interoperability recommendation, not confirmed MBR support for every current model.
Later model-specific filesystem, partition and firmware evidence takes precedence.
Official support states that CDJ/XDJ players read the first partition.
One usable data partition is a conservative preparation recommendation; this is not proof that every multi-partition drive is rejected.
Do not apply this statement to Denon/Engine hardware.
The model FAQ explicitly rejects GUID Partition Map.
A negative GPT statement does not positively confirm MBR; any MBR suggestion must retain its separate general-guidance label.
Firmware-update media require FAT/FAT32 even though playback also supports exFAT.
The official export guide lists FAT32 and exFAT for Windows, plus HFS+ for Mac.
Its exFAT list names only the specified newer models; do not extend it to all CDJ/XDJ units.
The guide lists supported formats rather than a universal preference: the FAT32 fallback here is a tool recommendation.
Existing model/firmware and rekordbox version advisories remain authoritative.
The PRIME 4 FAQ explicitly specifies FAT32 or exFAT with an MBR partition structure for connected media.
This confirms the manufacturer statement for PRIME 4; it is not a physical test and is not inherited by SC6000 or every Engine DJ model.
The separate internal-drive capacity answer is not a universal USB-capacity guarantee.
The model FAQ recommends exFAT for file systems of 1 TB or greater.
The byte threshold is a UI interpretation of the published TB wording, not a separately measured device boundary.
Do not silently switch a drive above the toolkit MBR limit to GPT or truncate capacity.
The generic formatting guide recommends GPT in the context of modern computer operating systems.
That generic advice conflicts with the PRIME 4 model FAQ if applied indiscriminately to player media.
It must not override model-specific MBR guidance or fill an unknown player partition capability.
The capacity FAQ states no fixed capacity limit for devices supporting its listed FAT/FAT32/HFS+ formats.
It supplies no tested byte ceiling, no cluster-size value and no proof that every controller or capacity works.
Do not interpret this as GPT support, an exFAT-specific capacity guarantee or permission to exceed the toolkit MBR limit.

clusterSizeBytes.reviewedScope: The listed official guides and FAQs; no numeric allocation-unit recommendation was located.

notes: The AlphaTheta first-partition guidance does not establish a universal one-partition hardware requirement.
No universal Engine DJ single-partition requirement was established by this bounded review.
The PRIME 4 FAQ cannot establish SC6000 partition compatibility.
The generic OS-formatting guide cannot establish a player-specific partition scheme.
Absence of a stated capacity ceiling is not an unlimited-capacity test result.
The toolkit MBR boundary is a separate implementation/safety limit.
